newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends lower on fund selling, meal mixed.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends lower on fund selling, meal mixed.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures ended lower on Thursday on active fund selling but losses were limited by commercial buying interest amid speculation of export business, traders said.
Soymeal futures ended mostly higher as funds bought at least 1,000 lots, traders said.
The fund selling dropped March soyoil futures as low as 23.66 cents per lb, down 0.32 cent from Wednesday's close. Prices recovered on commercial buying and oil/meal spreads.
Cargill Inc bought 300 lots March and Produce Grain bought 200 lots May and 100 lots each March and July.
One U.S. exporter told Reuters that China bought 24,000 tonnes U.S. soyoil for February 15-March 15 shipment.
Pit sources noted talk soyoil traded in Brazil at $514.00 per tonne for May, June or July shipment. That compared with U.S. Gulf FOB values at $530.00 per tonne for May shipment.
Bull spreads boosted nearby soymeal but news overnight that South Korea passed on its tender for 140,000 tonnes of soymeal due to high prices capped gains.
Soymeal closed $2.20 per ton lower to $1.70 higher with March up $1.70 at $248.80. Soyoil ended down 0.20 to 0.09 cent per lb with March off 0.14 at 23.84 cents.
Weekly export data lent some support to soy products early but traders quickly shrugged off the data, noting it reflected old news that had already been factored into the market.

USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of soymeal during the week ended February 6 totaled 119,300 tonnes, at the high end of trade expectations for 80,000 to 120,000 tonnes. Soyoil weekly exports were above expectations.

On the day, ADM sold 200 lots March soymeal and 100 lots May, traders said. Smith Barney bought 300 lots each March and May. In late dealings, ING, Merrill Lynch, Prudential Securities and Refco Inc were all buyers of the March.
In soyoil, Rosenthal Collins sold 1,000 lots March and R.J. O'Brien sold 300 lots May, floor sources said.

Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 30,000 lots. That compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 34,454 lots. Soyoil volume was estimated at 19,000 lots, against Wednesday's actual volume of 32,897 lots.
